games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which word is an action word, something you do?
rounds.explanation: Jump is something your body does; a table, rain and a shoe are naming words, not actions.

rounds.prompt: Which action do you do by putting your two hands together?
rounds.explanation: Clapping uses two hands; you run and jump with your legs and blink with your eyes.

rounds.prompt: A ball hits the ground and comes back up. Which word tells what it does?
rounds.explanation: Going down and up again is called bouncing; sleeping, eating and writing are not ball movements.

rounds.prompt: Sami throws a ball to Maya. What should Maya do with her hands?
rounds.explanation: You catch a ball that comes to you; throwing, dropping and hiding it would end the game.

rounds.prompt: Which word means to move very fast on your legs?
rounds.explanation: Running is fast leg movement; sitting is still, and looking and listening use your eyes and ears.

rounds.prompt: Which one is a question?
rounds.explanation: Only this one asks something and ends with a question mark; the others are telling sentences.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What colour was Amal's big ball?
choices: It went up into a big tree
Because he was tall and could shake the branch
rounds.explanation: The story says Amal had a big red ball.

rounds.prompt: In which town was Amal playing?
choices: On a branch of the big tree
rounds.explanation: The first line says it was a sunny day in the town of Hargeisa.

rounds.prompt: What happened to the ball after Leo threw it?
choices: It went up into a big tree
Sad, because the story says Leo looked sad
rounds.answer: It went up into a big tree
rounds.explanation: Leo threw the ball, it went up, up, up, and landed on a branch.

rounds.prompt: How did Leo feel when he asked to play? How do you know?
choices: Sad, because the story says Leo looked sad
Because he was tall and could shake the branch
rounds.answer: Sad, because the story says Leo looked sad
rounds.explanation: Leo asks 'Can I play too?' and the story says he looked sad.

rounds.prompt: Why could Adam get the ball down when the children could not?
choices: Because he was tall and could shake the branch
rounds.answer: Because he was tall and could shake the branch
rounds.explanation: The story says Adam was tall, and he shook the branch until the ball fell.

rounds.prompt: Which talk line tells where the ball is?
choices: It went up into a big tree
rounds.explanation: 'The ball is on the ___' is the position line in the talk lines.

games.title: Memory Pairs
games.description: Reveal tiles and connect each word with its meaning.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 1.
pairs: six
The number 6. It comes after five and before seven.
fin
A fin is the flat part on a fish that helps it swim.
run
To move your legs very fast, faster than walking.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 2.
pairs: do
We use do to ask questions and to talk about actions.
why
This word asks for the reason something happens.
puppy
A baby dog. It is soft and likes to play.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 3.
pairs: sad
Sad means you feel unhappy, like when something upsets you.
much
Much means a large amount of something.
window
A window is an opening in a wall that lets in light.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 4.
pairs: body
Your body is all the parts of you, like your arms, legs and head.
whee
Whee is a word you say when you feel a fun, fast rush of excitement.
roll
To move along by turning over and over.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 5.
pairs: hand
The part at the end of your arm with five fingers.
toes
The ten little parts at the end of your feet.
on
A small word that shows something is above and touching, like 'on the table'.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 6.
pairs: catch
To take hold of something moving in the air.
smile
A smile is the happy shape your mouth makes when you are pleased.
letter
A letter is one of the signs we use to write words, like a or b.
